claims.text: The proposed intervention is incorporation of approximately 1–2 vol% nanoscale Y2O3 into a refractory HEA using powder processing and spark plasma sintering.
A short aging treatment after spark plasma sintering will promote a uniform dispersion of Y2O3 nanoparticles in the HEA matrix.
Uniformly distributed Y2O3 nanoparticles will hinder dislocation motion in the refractory HEA.
Hindering dislocation motion with Y2O3 dispersoids will strengthen the refractory HEA.
Y2O3 dispersoids will act as stable sinks for irradiation-generated defects.
The Y2O3 dispersoids will not trigger deleterious phase transformations at elevated temperatures.
The Y2O3-modified refractory HEA will have higher yield strength than an otherwise comparable alloy without nano-oxide additions.
The Y2O3-modified refractory HEA will have improved toughness relative to the unmodified baseline.
The possible increase in yield strength is estimated to be approximately 10–20%.
The Y2O3-modified alloy will maintain high-temperature phase stability during service at approximately 800–1100 °C.
The Y2O3-modified alloy will maintain irradiation resistance during approximately 1 MeV ion irradiation.
The hypothesis is expected to apply to refractory HEAs processed by powder metallurgy and spark plasma sintering.
Substantially different alloy systems or Y2O3 volume fractions may require re-optimization.
